readout_other: extracellular single-unit recording of cerebellar Purkinje cell simple spikes
direction_notes: Purkinje cell simple spikes were entrained to the ultrasound pulse pattern with a probability peak shortly after pulse onset; overall firing rate was unchanged, and authors describe the immediate net effect as excitatory, though longer pulses produced a wider, delayed response suggesting an additional inhibitory component.

exposures.label: Cerebellar cortex sonication with varying pulse duration and PRF

timing.protocol_description: Ten-second-long neural recordings were collected and each second of recording contained 500 ms of ultrasound stimulation followed by 500 ms of no-stimulation period. The PRF was set to either 50 Hz or 100 Hz to make it close to the spontaneous firing rates of PCs. The pulse duration was adjusted to 0.5, 1, or 2 ms in sequential trials.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Six male Sprague Dawley rats (320e350 g) were used in this study.
